question.prompt: Each edge of a cube is colored either red or black. Every face of the cube has at least one black edge. The smallest possible number of black edges is

solutions.explanation:
First find a lower bound by counting how many faces each black edge can serve. Every edge of a cube belongs to exactly two faces. Thus, if there are \(b\) black edges, there are \(2b\) incidences between black edges and faces. Each of the six faces needs at least one such incidence, so
\[
2b\ge 6,
\]
and therefore \(b\ge 3\).

To show that three suffice, name the faces top, bottom, front, back, left, and right. Color black the edge shared by top and front, the edge shared by bottom and left, and the edge shared by back and right. These three edges serve all six faces, each exactly once. Color every other edge red.

The smallest possible number is therefore \(3\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: A bound and a construction
